title: NY State Senate · District 24
area: Most of Staten Island (Mid-Island and South Shore).

context.text: Neither candidate faced a primary. Incumbent Andrew Lanza has held this seat since 2007 and has won every general election since then with at least 78% of the vote; the district is the most Republican-leaning of the four covered here.

candidates.name: Andrew Lanza
candidates.currentRole: NY State Senator, District 24 (since 2007); Deputy Minority Leader

summary.text: Andrew Lanza is the Republican incumbent state senator for District 24, covering most of Staten Island, and has held the seat since 2007. A former Assistant District Attorney and New York City Council member, he serves as Deputy Minority Leader and sits on the Judiciary and Rules committees.

background.text: Earned a B.S. in accounting from St. John's University and a J.D. from Fordham University School of Law in 1992.
Worked as an Assistant District Attorney in the Manhattan office of Robert Morgenthau before entering elected office.
Served on the New York City Council before his election to the State Senate.
Authored the I-STOP prescription drug monitoring law and led the effort to establish the 13th Judicial District, consisting solely of Richmond County (Staten Island).

priorities.text: Has repeatedly sponsored legislation to incorporate a separate City of Staten Island.
Has focused on toll relief for Staten Island bridge commuters, including a bill capping cashless-tolling late fees and creating a toll amnesty program.

positions.summary: Criticized the state's Climate Leadership and Community Protection Act after a NYSERDA memo on its costs, saying the law is raising utility bills and that energy policy should not be driven by the push to cut fossil fuel use.
positions.quote: The leftist Democrat's radical and costly climate agenda was outed by NYSERDA's recent memo. Utility bills will continue to rise if we don't change course. Common sense should drive our State's energy policy, not climate activists who are damaging the quality of life and savings of New Yorkers.

positions.summary: Called Manhattan's congestion pricing program "this scheme" and said he hoped the incoming EPA administrator, whom he described as an opponent of the program, would help revisit it.
positions.quote: We're going to have a new EPA in Lee Zeldin, a good friend and opponent of this scheme.

record.text: Sponsored S8578, which would incorporate the City of Staten Island as its own municipality; in the Senate Cities 2 Committee as of the most recent action in the 2025-26 session.

Sponsored S9493, the "Toll Payer Advocacy and Relief Act," which would cap cashless-tolling late-payment penalties at 10%, require toll-authority advocate offices to respond to disputes within 48 hours, and create a toll amnesty program; referred to the Senate Corporations, Authorities and Commissions Committee on March 18, 2026.
Sponsored S9610, which would require elected county clerks and sheriffs in New York City; in the Senate Judiciary Committee as of the most recent action in the 2025-26 session.
Serves as Deputy Minority Leader and sits on the Cities 1, Ethics and Internal Governance, Judiciary, and Rules committees, and the Joint Senate and Assembly Commission on Legislative Ethics.

candidates.name: Alexis Rodriguez

summary.text: Alexis Rodriguez is the Democratic nominee challenging longtime incumbent Andrew Lanza in NY State Senate District 24.

candidates.researchNotes: Rodriguez has not completed a Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, and no news coverage of her platform could be located as of September 25, 2026. Her campaign website (alexisfornewyork.com) is linked from Ballotpedia but returns a bot-detection challenge page to automated fetches, so no verbatim quotes could be confirmed from it; her Instagram (@alexisfornewyork) and LinkedIn pages were likewise inaccessible to automated tools.
